notice: SYNTHETIC / FICTIONAL, hand-authored question bank and required elements for the demo deviation workflow (Examplon Pharma, fictional). Requirement IDs and SOP sections refer to the synthetic SOP set and public 21 CFR headings only.

elements.label: Description of event
elements.question: Describe what happened, factually.
elements.why: SOP-DEV-001 5.1 requires a factual description of the event.

elements.label: Site
elements.question: At which site did the event happen?
elements.why: The deviation record identifies the site (SOP-DEV-001 5.1).

elements.label: Product or material
elements.question: Which product or material is involved?
elements.why: The deviation record identifies the product (SOP-DEV-001 5.1).

elements.label: Lot / batch number
elements.question: Which lot or batch is involved?
elements.why: Batch record review needs the affected lot (21 CFR 211.192; SOP-DEV-001 5.1).

elements.label: Equipment
elements.question: Which equipment is involved?
elements.why: The deviation record identifies the equipment (SOP-DEV-001 5.1).

elements.label: Date discovered
elements.question: On what date was the event discovered?
elements.why: SOP-DEV-001 5.1: report within 24 hours of detection; the detection date starts that clock.

elements.label: Date of event
elements.question: On what date did the event occur (if different from the date discovered)?
elements.why: The form requires the event date as well as the detection date (SOP-DEV-001 5.1).

elements.label: Reported by
elements.question: Who is reporting this event?
elements.why: The originator reports the event (SOP-DEV-001 section 4).

elements.label: Immediate action / containment
elements.question: What immediate action or containment was taken?
elements.why: Written procedures for deviations require containment to be recorded (21 CFR 211.100; SOP-DEV-001 5.2).

elements.label: Event type
elements.question: Confirm or change the event type.
elements.why: The record type selects the template and the questions asked (SOP-DEV-001 5.1).

elements.label: Classification
elements.question: Confirm or change the classification (minor / major / critical).
elements.why: QA classifies each deviation using the SOP-DEV-002 criteria (SOP-DEV-001 5.3). A person must record this decision.

elements.label: Applicable regulations
elements.question: Confirm or change the applicable requirements.
elements.why: The draft cites the requirements the event relates to.

elements.label: Applicable SOPs
elements.question: Confirm or change the applicable SOPs.
elements.why: The draft cites the procedures that govern the event.

elements.label: Root cause
elements.question: What is the root cause? Give a preliminary statement, or record 'to be determined at investigation'.
elements.why: A documented root cause is needed to close a deviation (21 CFR 211.192; SOP-DEV-001 5.4; SOP-INV-001 4). A person must record this decision.

elements.label: Product impact
elements.question: What is the product impact (no_impact / potential_impact / confirmed_impact)?
elements.why: QA documents the product and batch impact assessment (21 CFR 211.192; SOP-DEV-001 5.5). A person must record this decision.

elements.label: Reportability
elements.question: Is the event reportable (not_reportable / potentially_reportable / reportable)?
elements.why: Reportability needs an explicit recorded human decision (URS AI-05).

elements.label: CAPA decision
elements.question: Is a CAPA needed, and if not, why not?
elements.why: A CAPA is raised when a root cause needs a systemic fix; a correction alone needs the decision recorded (SOP-CAPA-001 4; 21 CFR 211.22).

elements.label: Recurrence check
elements.question: Has the same event type occurred on the same equipment or product in the last 24 months?
elements.why: QA checks the deviation history for recurrence (SOP-DEV-002 5).

elements.label: Lot disposition
elements.question: What is the proposed disposition of each affected lot (release / rework / reject)?
elements.why: QA decides the disposition of every affected lot once impact is possible (SOP-DEV-001 5.5; 21 CFR 211.192).

elements.label: Other affected lots
elements.question: Which other lots, products or equipment could be affected?
elements.why: The impact assessment covers other lots, products and equipment (SOP-DEV-001 5.5).

elements.label: Notification plan
elements.question: Who must be notified, by when, and who owns the notification?
elements.why: A reportable or potentially reportable event needs a notification plan (URS AI-05 decision follow-up).

elements.label: Patient safety assessment
elements.question: Is there a confirmed or probable impact on patient safety? State the basis.
elements.why: A critical classification rests on patient-safety impact or a failed critical quality attribute (SOP-DEV-002 3).

elements.label: Equipment status
elements.question: What is the current status of the equipment (tagged out, repaired, re-qualified)?
elements.why: Equipment must be controlled after a failure (21 CFR 211.68; SOP-DEV-001 5.2).

elements.label: Laboratory phase 1 review
elements.question: Has the laboratory phase 1 review for an assignable cause been done? What was found?
elements.why: Laboratory OOS results follow a phase 1 then phase 2 investigation (SOP-INV-001 5; 21 CFR 211.160).

elements.label: Supplier notification
elements.question: Has the supplier been notified, and has the affected material been quarantined?
elements.why: Containment covers segregating affected material (SOP-DEV-001 5.2).

elements.label: Training status
elements.question: Was the person's training on the current procedure version complete before the event?
elements.why: Missing training is a documented root-cause category (SOP-INV-001 4).

elements.label: Records affected
elements.question: Which batch or control records or pages are affected?
elements.why: Batch and control records must be complete (21 CFR 211.188, 211.180).
